messaging_implications.implication: Lead with the most frequent pain, in the customer's words: "Scheduling takes hours every week." (2 docs)
Frame the promise around the outcome customers ask for: "I just want something simple so that I can stop doing it manually." (1 doc)
Answer the top objection before the CTA: "Honestly it looks good but it's too expensive for a small shop like mine, not sure it's worth it." (1 doc)
Reduce choices and jargon: one primary CTA, one plan highlighted, plain language
Anchor price against the cost of the problem or current workaround; show what is included
Address switching effort explicitly (setup time, migration help, no lock-in if true)
Test loss-framed messaging (what the current situation costs) against gain framing

output.segments_note: Single profile built from pooled inputs. If inputs mix segments (e.g. owners vs staff, new vs returning), run build_profile per segment: triggers and objections usually differ.
